newsitem.title: USA: Diamond to unveil fast multimedia products.
newsitem.headline: Diamond to unveil fast multimedia products.

text.p: Diamond Multimedia Systems Inc. plans this week to unveil several new marketing initiatives for enhanced video and audio technologies.
On Monday, the company said it will launch a deal with Toshiba Corp.'s Toshiba America Information Systems unit to deliver what will be among the first DVD-ROM products to hit the retail market.
Diamond will also announce new proprietary 3-D audio software and plans for moving into the market for machines running Microsoft Corp.'s Windows NT system.

On Tuesday, the San Jose, Calif. maker of multimedia accelerators, modems and adopters also plans to launch new plug- and-play video conferencing product, including a color camera and a microphone, at an estimated retail price of $399.

Amid the flurry of introductions ahead of the annual Comdex computer industry trade show beginning Nov. 17, Diamond Multimedia's Chief Executive Bill Schroeder said in an interview that the company is on track to increase its revenues and margins in its current fourth quarter.
"Our expectation is that in the fourth quarter versus the third quarter that our revenues and margins will expand," he said. "Fundamentally, we expect to be profitable."

Diamond last month reported sales of $123.7 million for the three months to Sept. 29, with a gross profit of 25 million, operating profit of $2.7 million and net income of $2.1 million, or six cents a share.

Schroeder also said that Diamond's revenues, which hit $467 million in 1995 and have already reached $431.6 million for the first nine months of 1996, appear on target for analysts' estimates of roughly $600 million for full-year 1996.
"Wall Street has that as an estimate of what we'll do this year, and that seems a reasonable estimate for what we're going to do," he said, declining to provide further details.

Under its partnership with Toshiba, Diamond will provide its PCI-based adapters, including decoders for the MPEG-2 video standard and Dolby AC-3 digital audio capabilities, for commercial and retail distribution as multimedia upgrade kits.

DVD, or digital video disk, technology provides high-speed data transfer which is capable of storing seven times the amount data on a CD-ROM. A double-sided, double layer DVD disk can store around 25 times a CD-ROM's capacity.
Diamond expects the technology to pick up momentum next year, and become a predominant local storage device by 2000.
